cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.metaTitle: Cookie Policy · Bag Of Holding Tools

s1.heading: 1. What is a cookie?
s1.p1: A cookie is a small file placed on your browser when you visit a site. This page explains which cookies and storage technologies are used by Bag Of Holding Tools and its tools, including Dynasty Tree Builder (the "Site").
s1.p2: The Site uses no advertising, social-media or personalization cookies. Your activity is never sold or used for commercial purposes. Only audience measurement, described in section 4, may be switched on — and only if you explicitly accept it.

s2.heading: 2. Strictly necessary cookies
s2.p1: These cookies are strictly necessary for the Site to function. Under the applicable rules, they do not require your consent.
s2.item1: Supabase session cookie (e.g. sb-…-auth-token) — keeps you signed in to your account. Only set if you create an account and sign in. Duration: until you sign out or the session expires.

s3.heading: 3. Local storage (guest mode)
s3.p1: In guest mode (no account), the Site uses your browser's local storage (localStorage) to save your work on your own device. This data is never sent to our servers and is deleted when you clear your browser storage. This mechanism is strictly necessary and does not require your consent.
s3.p2: Your answer to the consent request described in section 4 is kept there too (key boh-analytics-consent), so that you are not asked again on every visit. That record is strictly necessary as well: without it, a refusal could not be honoured.

s4.heading: 4. Audience measurement (subject to your consent)
s4.p1: With your prior agreement, the Site uses Google Analytics 4 to measure traffic: number of visits, pages viewed, approximate origin and device type. We use it only to learn which tools are worth building on.
s4.item1: _ga and _ga_stream id — distinguish visitors and sessions. Duration: 13 months at most.
s4.p2: Nothing is set until you accept. If you decline, or simply do not answer, no audience-measurement cookie is created and no data is sent to Google. The Site works exactly the same either way: no feature is conditional on your acceptance.
s4.p3: The content you create — characters, relationships, trees, notes — is never sent to Google. Google acts as a processor; data may be transferred to the United States under the conditions described in section 9 of the Privacy Policy.

s5.heading: 5. Cookies not used
s5.p1: For transparency, the following categories are never used by the Site:
items: Selling or sharing your data for commercial purposes — none

s6.heading: 6. Managing your browser
s6.p1: You can configure your browser at any time to block or delete cookies. Note: without the session cookie, you will not be able to stay signed in to your account. To learn more, see the CNIL website: <cnil>cnil.fr</cnil>.

preamble.heading: Preamble
preamble.p1: This policy applies to all tools published under Bag Of Holding Tools, including Dynasty Tree Builder. All tools share the same account system, so one policy covers all of them. It explains how your personal data is collected, processed and retained, in accordance with French Law no. 78-17 of 6 January 1978 ("Informatique et Libertés") and Regulation (EU) 2016/679 ("GDPR").

s1.heading: 1. Definition
s1.p1: "Personal data" means any information that can identify you directly or indirectly, such as your email address.

s2.heading: 2. Data controller
s2.p1: The data controller is the Site's publisher: an individual acting on a personal and non-commercial basis, publishing under the pseudonym {alias} in accordance with article 6-III-2 of the French LCEN ("We"). Their full details are held by the host.
s2.p2: The data controller can be reached at any time at <mail>{email}</mail>. That address is the single point of contact for every request concerning your data.

s3.heading: 3. Guest mode (no account)
s3.p1: You can use every tool without creating an account. In guest mode, your data (characters, relationships and any content you create) is stored only in your browser (localStorage) and is never sent to our servers. Exporting to PNG or JSON happens entirely on your device. We have no access to guest-mode data.
s3.p2: Guest mode is not exempt from the optional audience measurement described in section 5. That covers browsing only (pages viewed, device type), never the content you create, and it stays off until you have accepted it.

s4.heading: 4. Data collected and purposes (account mode)
s4.p1: Creating an account is optional and only exists to save your work to the cloud. When you sign in with Google, we collect:
items: The data you create in each tool (e.g. characters, relationships, roles and custom names for Dynasty Tree Builder).
s4.p2: We do not collect your name, profile picture, or any other Google account data beyond your email address. The legal basis for this processing is the performance of the contract you enter into by creating an account. Your data is used solely to identify you and let you access your work across sessions and devices.

s5.heading: 5. Recipients and subprocessors
s5.p1: Your account data is processed by the following providers, solely to operate the service:
s5.item4: Google Analytics — audience measurement, only if you have accepted it. Nothing is sent to it before you agree, and your content is never sent to it at all. See the Cookie Policy.
s5.p2: Your data is never sold, rented, or shared with any third party beyond these providers.

s6.heading: 6. Data retention
s6.p1: Account data is retained for as long as your account exists. You may request deletion of your account and all associated data at any time by writing to <mail>{email}</mail>. Deletion is permanent.

s7.heading: 7. Security
s7.p1: We implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to preserve the security, integrity and confidentiality of your data and to prevent unauthorized third-party access.

s8.heading: 8. Hosting
s8.p1: Your account data is stored on Supabase servers, in a region located within the European Union.

s9.heading: 9. Transfers outside the European Union
s9.p1: Vercel and Google are based in the United States. Where your data is transferred outside the European Union, that transfer is covered either by an adequacy decision (including the EU–US Data Privacy Framework) or by the standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission.

s10.heading: 10. Your rights
s10.p1: Under the GDPR, you have the following rights:
items: Right of access, rectification and erasure of your data;
Right to data portability (receive your data in a machine-readable format);
Right to withdraw your consent at any time;
Right to define directives on what happens to your data after your death.
s10.p2: You can exercise these rights by writing to <mail>{email}</mail>. We reply within one month of receiving your request.

s11.heading: 11. Complaint to a supervisory authority
s11.p1: You have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in France the <cnil>CNIL</cnil> — if you believe the processing of your data breaches applicable law.

s12.heading: 12. Data about third parties
s12.p1: Some tools let you enter information about other people (for example family members). You are responsible for having the right to enter that information — see our <terms>Terms of Use</terms>. If a third party wants information about them removed from an account they do not control, they can contact us and we will forward the request to the account holder or act on it directly where required by law.

s13.heading: 13. Children
s13.p1: Our tools are not directed at children under 15. If you believe a child under 15 has created an account, contact us and we will delete it.

s14.heading: 14. Changes
s14.p1: We may update this policy as tools are added or changed. Changes take effect upon publication, reflected in the last-updated date above.

home.metaTitle: Dynasty Tree Builder — D&D & TTRPG Family Tree Maker
home.metaDescription: A free family tree maker for D&D and TTRPG campaigns. Map noble houses, NPC relationships, bloodlines and rivalries on a drag-and-drop canvas, then share a link or export a PNG. No account needed.

hero.heading: Every noble house is a <accent>web of blood and betrayal</accent>. Map yours.
hero.lede: A free family tree maker for D&D and TTRPG campaigns — characters, bloodlines, partnerships and the rivalries your players keep tripping over.
hero.note: Guest mode saves in your browser — sign in only to sync across devices.

beats.title: It starts with one name
beats.body: Open the canvas and add a founder. No account, no setup, no empty-project wizard — a card on a dark ground and somewhere to put the next one.

beats.title: Then the house complicates
beats.body: Add partners, children, second marriages. The layout engine keeps generations in bands and packs siblings together, so the shape stays readable while you improvise. Bastards, adoptions and exiles are flags, not workarounds.

beats.title: Until it has a shape you can hand to your players
beats.body: Hover any character to light their whole bloodline. Publish and you get a read-only link — the live canvas, no account needed at their end — or export the tree as a PNG for the campaign wiki.

what.heading: A dynasty generator for tabletop campaigns
what.p1: Most family tree software is built for genealogy: real ancestors, birth certificates, dates you can verify. Campaign families are messier. Half the parents are unknown, a third of the heirs are secretly bastards, two houses married for a treaty that has since collapsed, and the whole thing has to stay legible while you improvise at the table.
what.p2: Dynasty Tree Builder is a fantasy family tree builder made for that. You drop characters onto a canvas, link them as parents, partners or adopted children, and the layout engine arranges the generations for you. Every character carries a role and a set of narrative flags, so the tree doubles as a campaign NPC relationship map rather than just a chart of who begat whom.
what.p3: It runs in the browser, it is free, and you'll be building within ten seconds — <canvas>open the canvas as a guest</canvas> and see.

items.title: A canvas built for lineages
items.body: Drag characters around an infinite canvas. Generations snap into horizontal bands and siblings pack tightly, so a ten-generation house reads top to bottom without crossing lines.

items.title: Relationships that mean something
items.body: Connect people as parent/child, partner or adopted. Each relationship type draws its own edge style, and every link can carry a plot hook — the reason this connection matters at the table.

items.title: Roles and narrative flags
items.body: Give a character a role (Head of House, Heir, Consort, Rival, Mage, Rogue…) and stack permanent flags on top: founder, bastard, adopted, exile, deceased. Signed-in users can add their own custom roles.

items.title: Share a read-only link
items.body: Publish a dynasty and hand your players a link. They get the live canvas — pan, zoom, highlight a bloodline — with no ability to edit and no account of their own. Unpublish whenever the secret stops being a secret.

items.title: PNG export
items.body: Export the tree as a high-resolution PNG cropped to your characters. Works from the editor and from a shared view, so players can grab their own copy for the campaign wiki.

items.title: Guest mode, no signup
items.body: Open the canvas and start building. Guest dynasties live in your browser's local storage. Create an account only when you want the tree on more than one device — your guest work can be imported.

items.title: Dungeon masters
items.body: Keep the NPC relationship map for a court intrigue arc in one place. When a player asks who the duke's half-brother married, you have the answer on screen instead of buried three sessions back in your notes.

items.title: Worldbuilders
items.body: Trace a founding bloodline across centuries, split it into cadet branches, and mark which lines died out. The generation bands make the shape of a dynasty's rise and collapse visible at a glance.

items.title: Players with a backstory
items.body: Map your character's house before session one — who raised them, who disowned them, which cousin holds the title now. Share the link with your DM so the details survive contact with the campaign.

items.title: Writers and play-by-post groups
items.body: Nothing here is D&D-specific. Any story with a succession, a feud or a tangled family works: sci-fi houses, horror bloodlines, historical fiction, or a novel's cast you keep losing track of.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.jsonLdName: Dynasty Tree Builder — frequently asked questions

items.a: Yes. Building, sharing and exporting dynasty trees is free, with no trial period and no payment details. Signing in is optional and only exists so your trees follow you between devices.

items.q: Do I need an account to make a family tree?
items.a: No. Guest mode opens straight onto the canvas and saves your dynasty in your own browser's local storage. If you later create an account, the tree you built as a guest can be imported into it.

items.q: Can I use it for D&D, Pathfinder or a homebrew system?
items.a: Yes. Nothing in the tool is tied to a ruleset. Characters carry a name, an optional alias, a role and narrative flags, so it works for any tabletop RPG, play-by-post game or novel-writing project.

items.q: How do I share a dynasty tree with my players?
items.a: Publish the dynasty and you get a read-only share link. Anyone with the link sees the same canvas — pan, zoom, follow bloodlines and export a PNG — but cannot change anything. Unpublish at any time to break the link.

items.q: Can I export the family tree as an image?
items.a: Yes. One click exports the whole canvas as a high-resolution PNG that crops to your characters, so you can drop it into a campaign wiki, a Discord channel, a session handout or a VTT.

items.q: How many characters can one dynasty hold?
items.a: There is no fixed cap. The layout engine places generations in bands and packs siblings together, so large houses spanning many generations stay readable instead of turning into a tangle of crossing lines.

items.q: Does it handle bastards, adoptions and multiple partners?
items.a: Yes. A character can have several partners, each with their own offspring line, and children can be marked as adopted or as bastards. Unknown parents can be left as placeholder nodes so an incomplete lineage still renders correctly.

closing.heading: Map your first house
closing.body: No signup, no trial, no card. Open the canvas, add a founder, and start branching.
